name: Moshi
description: Speech-text foundation model and full-duplex spoken dialogue framework with inner monologue text prediction for natural conversations
use_case: Real-time voice conversation with LLMs, full-duplex dialogue, speech-text interaction
key_features: Mimi neural codec (24 kHz, 1.1 kbps, 80ms latency)
notes: Most mature production-ready voice project; recommended for Obsidian integration as primary voice backend

name: Pocket TTS
description: Lightweight text-to-speech that runs on CPU without GPU or web API dependency, featuring voice cloning
use_case: Low-resource TTS, voice cloning, on-device speech synthesis
key_features: 6x faster than real-time on MacBook Air M4
Multiple interfaces: CLI, Python API, HTTP server
notes: Best for resource-constrained environments; excellent for Obsidian note-to-speech features; English only

name: Unmute
description: Voice-enabled system allowing any LLM to listen and speak in real-time conversations with low-latency streaming
use_case: Voice interface for LLMs, real-time conversation, multimodal AI assistants
key_features: Works with any OpenAI-compatible LLM server
Multiple deployment options: Docker Compose, Dockerless, Docker Swarm
dependencies: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support (minimum 16GB VRAM)
Docker Compose and NVIDIA Container Toolkit
Linux or Windows with WSL (Mac unsupported)
notes: Production-ready deployment framework; key for Obsidian plugin voice interface; GPU-dependent

name: Delayed Streams Modeling
description: Speech-To-Text and Text-To-Speech models using Delayed Streams Modeling framework with word-level timestamps and semantic VAD
use_case: Real-time STT/TTS, streaming speech processing, low-latency voice applications
key_features: STT models: 1B (~0.5s delay) and 2.6B (~2.5s delay) parameter versions
Real-time streaming inference with efficient batching
Semantic VAD (voice activity detection) in 1B model
notes: Core speech processing component; essential for both STT and TTS pipelines in MCP server

name: Hibiki
description: Streaming speech translation system for real-time simultaneous translation with voice transfer capability
use_case: Real-time speech translation, simultaneous interpretation, multilingual voice applications
key_features: Multistream architecture for source/target speech modeling
dependencies: PyTorch, MLX, MLX-Swift, or Rust runtime
notes: French-to-English only; excellent for international collaboration features; mobile-ready implementation

name: MoshiVis
description: Vision-language model extending Moshi with multimodal image understanding for visual conversation
use_case: Image understanding in voice conversations, visual Q&A, multimodal voice interface
license: CC-BY 4.0 (weights, excluding vision) + Gemma License (vision) + MIT (Python) + Apache-2.0 (Rust)
key_features: ~206M adapter parameters added to 7B Moshi model
Gating mechanisms for visual input modulation
Multiple backends: PyTorch (BF16), Rust/Candle (Q8), MLX (Q4/Q8 quantization)
notes: Adds vision to Moshi conversations; training code planned for release; excellent for note-with-image features

name: CASA (Cross-Attention via Self-Attention)
description: Efficient vision-language fusion model with improved cross-attention mechanism for real-time streaming inference
use_case: Vision-language understanding, document analysis, live video captioning, visual QA
license: MIT (code) + CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 (model weights) + Qwen Research License (Qwen components)
key_features: Benchmark evaluation on documents, charts, visual QA
Natural gating mechanism for vision integration
notes: Novel architecture for efficient vision-language fusion; training code planned; good for Obsidian image features

name: Invincible Voice
description: Voice communication system for people with speech disabilities, enabling natural conversations with LLM-powered responses
use_case: Assistive technology, accessibility, voice for speech-disabled individuals
key_features: Multiple LLM response generation with user selection
Full user agency in conversation flow
notes: Accessibility-focused; under active development with online version planned; strong social impact focus

name: Flashy
description: Lightweight deep learning training framework emphasizing simplicity and hackability with built-in experiment management
use_case: Research deep learning workflows, model training, experiment management
notes: Essential infrastructure for Kyutai model training; core dependency for model development work

name: Dora
description: Experiment management system for expressing and executing large-scale hyperparameter grid searches across clusters
use_case: ML experiment tracking, hyperparameter optimization, distributed training coordination
key_features: Grid search as pure Python files
Automatic deduplication via unique hash signatures
notes: Infrastructure tool for research workflows; core for model training pipelines; excellent for Ollama MCP integration

name: ARC-Encoder
description: Adaptable text Representations Compressor for learning compressed text representations that reduce LLM computational requirements
use_case: Text compression, efficient LLM inference, context compression, token reduction
notes: Advanced compression techniques; useful for optimizing context in Ollama MCP; retrieval module is non-commercial

name: SPHN
description: Python bindings for Symphonia and Opus audio processing libraries, enabling efficient audio file manipulation
use_case: Audio codec operations, audio format conversion, audio data preprocessing
key_features: Load multiple audio formats into NumPy arrays
notes: Low-level audio infrastructure; essential for Mimi codec integration and audio pipeline

name: nanoGPTaudio
description: Implementation demonstrating techniques for integrating audio into language models through neural audio codecs
use_case: Audio codec training, audio-LLM integration research, audio tokenization
notes: Research code with hardcoded paths; will not work out-of-box; useful reference for audio-LLM integration concepts
